alice: Heads-up — our public launch is scheduled for next Fri (change window 08:00-18:00 UTC). Need to confirm freeze rules + hotfix exemption flow.
ben: Thanks — are we keeping the standard 72h code freeze for non-critical changes?
carla: Yes. 72h for all code/config changes to services in the release surface. Exceptions require a documented emergency request and 2x approvers from product + eng.
dinesh: For infra-only tweaks (scaling, autoscale config) do those count as non-critical? We sometimes need last-minute capacity tuning.
alice: Infra tweaks are allowed until 6h before window start, but any change must be tagged `release-exempt` and have a rollback plan in PR description.
emily: Suggest we codify a small exemption process to avoid churn. Maybe a single-form flow and a channel tag so oncall sees it.
carla: +1. We can use the existing Release Exemptions doc and a short Slack workflow: `#eng-releases` -> `/request-exemption` -> triage by oncall -> approvals logged.
alice: Draft process (short):
```
- submit /request-exemption with: owner, urgency, risk, rollback link
- oncall triages within 30m
- need product + eng lead approval for P2/P1
- deploy gated to canary then monitor 30m
```
Can we live with that?
dinesh: Works. For canary percentages I'd like 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 45m with automatic rollback on error budget hit.
ben: Agree on canary. Also: pinning — we must pin model and runtime versions for the launch traffic. Has ops created the pin manifest?
carla: I created a pin manifest PR #4123 yesterday. It pins model v2.1.0-quant to the prod profile and runtime 3.4.2. Please review.
emily: I'll review PR 4123 now. Reminder: include evaluation hash and perf baseline in the PR body so Optimize team can verify.
deploy-bot: deploy requested by alice: `release/v1.0.0` -> staged-canary at 1923456795
launch-bot: canary started: 5% traffic routed to release/v1.0.0 at 1923456796
alice: Oncall @dinesh, please watch error budget and latency panels for the next 60m and call abort on any sustained SLO breach.
dinesh: Watching now. Setting dashboard alert thresholds at +20% latency and 1.5x error rate baseline.
carla: If canary passes, we follow the rollout policy: 20% after 15m, 50% after 30m, full after 45m — manual go at each step.
emily: One more: exemption approvals must be recorded in the PR and a short note in this thread (copy/paste) for audit.
ben: Rollback plan (short):
```
- stop rollout
- revert traffic to previous tag
- trigger emergency patch branch: hotfix/<issue>
- postmortem trigger if >30m degradation
```
alice: OK — process looks good. Final checklist before freeze: 
- PRs merged that touch release surface: confirm 72h
- Pin manifest merged: #4123
- Exemption form live and triage rota set
- Ops oncall confirmed (dinesh)
- Rollback doc link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback
carla: I merged #4123.
ben: Exemption workflow created and added to Slack (/request-exemption).
dinesh: Oncall roster updated. I'll respond to exemptions within 30m.
emily: Reviewed performance baselines in PR. All good.
launch-bot: canary at 5% stable for 35m, no SLO breaches detected at 1923456840
deploy-bot: rollout to 20% requested by alice at 1923456845
launch-bot: rollout to 20% complete at 1923456846
alice: Great — team, this thread stands as the launch-readiness record. If anyone approves an exemption after freeze starts, paste approval here with PR link.
carla: Noted. I'll update audit log after any exemption. :white_check_mark:
emily: Copy.

---
Notes: keep this thread short and use /request-exemption for anything during freeze. Any post-freeze hotfixes must follow the rollback playbook above.
